name: Elements and the periodic table trends

questions.q: How are elements arranged in the modern periodic table?
a: In order of increasing atomic number
In alphabetical order of their symbols
In order of decreasing atomic mass

questions.q: What name is given to the vertical columns in the periodic table?
What do elements in the same group of the periodic table share in common?
a: They have the same number of total electron shells
They have the same number of valence electrons, resulting in similar chemical properties
They are all gases at room temperature

questions.q: What do horizontal rows in the periodic table represent?
a: Periods, indicating the number of electron shells

questions.q: Which group of elements in the periodic table is known as the alkali metals?
Which group contains the halogens, which are reactive non-metals?
Why are the noble gases (Group 0) notoriously unreactive?
a: They are solids at room temperature
They possess a full outer shell of electrons, making them stable
They consist entirely of radioactive isotopes

questions.q: How does reactivity change as you go down Group 1 (alkali metals)?
How does reactivity change as you go down Group 7 (halogens)?
a: It becomes identical to noble gases

questions.q: What physical trend in melting points is observed as you descend Group 7 (from fluorine to iodine)?
a: Melting points and boiling points increase as you go down
Melting points drop to absolute zero

questions.q: Which of the following elements is a transition metal found in the central block of the periodic table?
What trend in metallic character is observed across a period from left to right in the periodic table?
a: Metallic character decreases as elements transition from metals to non-metals

questions.q: Which alkali metal reacts most vigorously with water among lithium, sodium, and potassium?
a: They all react at the exact same speed

questions.q: What is formed when a halogen reacts with a metal, such as chlorine reacting with sodium?
Which halogen is a dark grey-black solid at room temperature that sublimes into a purple vapor when heated?
Why do atoms of elements in the same group have similar chemical properties?
a: They have the same atomic mass
They have the same number of neutrons
They have the same physical color
They have the same number of electrons in their outermost shell

questions.q: Which scientist is credited with developing the early periodic table by arranging elements by atomic mass and leaving gaps for undiscovered elements?
What is the physical state of bromine at room temperature?
As you move down Group 1, what happens to the density and melting points of the metals?
a: Melting points and softness generally decrease/increase respectively (melting points decrease down the group)

questions.q: Which group 2 element is commonly known as an alkaline earth metal?
What property distinguishes transition metals from Group 1 alkali metals?
a: Transition metals are typically harder, stronger, have higher melting points, and form colored compounds
Transition metals react instantly with cold water
Transition metals have only one electron in their outer shell

questions.q: What happens when chlorine water is added to a solution of potassium bromide?
a: Bromine is displaced, turning the solution orange-brown
An explosion shatters the test tube

questions.q: Which term describes elements that lie along the zig-zag line between metals and non-metals, possessing properties of both?
Why does atomic radius generally decrease as you move across a period from left to right?
a: The outermost electrons are repelled away
The nuclear charge (number of protons) increases, pulling the electron shells closer

questions.q: Which of the following gases glows with a characteristic color when high voltage is applied, typical of noble gases?
What type of oxides are formed when period 3 non-metals (like sulfur or phosphorus) react with oxygen?
What type of oxides are formed when period 3 metals (like sodium or magnesium) react with oxygen?
Which of the following halogens is a pale yellow gas at room temperature?
In terms of electron configuration, what do all elements in Period 3 have in common?
a: They all have three occupied electron shells
They all have three valence electrons
They all have completely full outer shells
They all have identical chemical reactivity

questions.q: Why can a more reactive halogen displace a less reactive halogen from an aqueous solution of its salt?
a: It has a greater attraction for electrons/higher oxidizing strength than the lower halogen
It is physically larger in size

questions.q: What is the primary reason why alkali metals must be stored under oil?
a: To prevent them from reacting rapidly with moisture and oxygen in the air

questions.q: Which of the following elements has the lowest electronegativity and highest reactivity within Group 1?
How many electrons are found in the outer shell of a neutral atom of a Group 2 element?
Which property correctly describes transition metal catalysts?
a: They speed up chemical reactions without being permanently consumed
They cool down the reaction mixture

questions.q: What trend is observed in the boiling points of the noble gases (Group 0) as you go down the group?
a: Boiling points decrease to absolute zero
Boiling points increase as atomic size and intermolecular forces increase

questions.q: Which of the following is an accurate description of silicon, a metalloid in Period 3?
a: It is a liquid metal at room temperature
It is a highly reactive Group 1 alkali metal
It is a colored halogen gas
It is a semiconductor with properties intermediate between metals and non-metals

questions.q: What happens to the pH of the resulting solution when sodium oxide is dissolved in water?
What happens to the pH of the resulting solution when sulfur dioxide gas is dissolved in water?
a: It becomes acidic due to the formation of sulfurous acid

questions.q: Which of the following elements is classified as a non-metal liquid at room temperature?
Why does fluorine have a higher reactivity than iodine within Group 7?
a: Fluorine's outer shell is closer to the nucleus, allowing it to gain an electron more easily
